core_obligations: One direction (proof line 11986): if the first topology is contained in the second then every sheaf for the second is a sheaf for the first, directly from the definitions.

The comparison of sheafifications (proof lines 11987-11999): from the inclusion of the categories of sheaves the author obtains a canonical comparison between the two sheafification functors, and identifies the second sheafification as the sheafification of the first with respect to the larger topology.

The conclusion (proof lines 12000-12018): applying this to the inclusion of a sieve generated by a covering of the first topology and using the criterion characterizing covering sieves by sheafification, the author concludes that the sieve is also covering for the second topology.
proof_roadmap: The easy direction is direct from the definitions.
Build the comparison between the two sheafifications from the inclusion of the categories of sheaves.
Apply it to the sieve generated by a covering and use the sheafification criterion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes the inclusion of one topology in another by the inclusion of the corresponding categories of sheaves in the reverse direction (statement lines 11978-11983). The proof is a complete argument: one direction is immediate (proof line 11986); from the inclusion of the categories of sheaves the author obtains a canonical comparison between the two sheafification functors and identifies the second as the sheafification of the first (proof lines 11987-11999); and applying this to the sieve generated by a covering, together with the criterion characterizing covering sieves by sheafification, shows that such a sieve is covering for the larger topology (proof lines 12000-12018). The non-formal content is the comparison of the two sheafifications. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
